ruling: ADR_UGENCE_LIVE_MODEL_PROVIDER_COMMISSIONING.md ballot LP-1 to LP-6 (PENDING the owner's rulings); OWNER_RATIFICATION_LIVE_MODEL_PROVIDER.md D-1 to D-5 (ratified 2026-09-10, standing)
status_note: On 2026-09-11 the owner designated the vendor (OpenAI) and the secret manager (Google Secret Manager). The rulings LP-1 to LP-6 have not been issued, the remaining designations are UNDESIGNATED, and nothing below commissions anything: no credential exists in any Ugence deployment, no MEU deployment unit exists (CR-1), and MEU_LIVE_VALIDATION.json is BLOCKED_PENDING_OWNER_RULINGS. Every field here is configuration or a placeholder, never a secret.

vendor.name: OpenAI
vendor.permitted_egress: https://api.openai.com only, from the Model Egress Unit deployment unit once CR-1 admits it (LP-1); the governed runtime worker's egress record is unchanged and names no vendor host
vendor.model: UNDESIGNATED (LP-3: exactly one model identifier; the adapter reads authorized_model from the authorization binding and hardcodes none)
vendor.account: UNDESIGNATED (LP-3: a non-production account with a hard spending cap set at the vendor; recorded as a reference, never as a key)

custody.secret_name: UNDESIGNATED (a reference of the form projects/<project>/secrets/<name>; versions are leased by number and recorded as secret_version_ref)
custody.rotation_policy: UNDESIGNATED (LP-2: a maximum credential age and rotation on any suspected exposure, asserted by the custody adapter as max_credential_age)
custody.audit_trail: every materialization, granted or refused, is a CustodyAuditEvent of identifiers and digests appended under meu.credential_leased / meu.credential_refused (ledger_kinds.py); the secret is never a field of any record
custody.meu_identity_to_secret_manager: UNRULED (LP-2a): how the Model Egress Unit authenticates to Google Secret Manager. A long-lived service-account key held on the hosting platform is itself a credential in the deployment and is refused under D-3; the candidate is workload identity federation from an identity the hosting platform issues, which the platform must support; failing that, the custody adapter runs on an owner-operated host, as the AP-3 verifier did
custody.port: ugence_model_egress_unit.custody.ModelCredentialCustodyPort; the only adapter in this distribution is ReferenceCustodyAdapter (FIXTURE_ONLY, never production-authoritative, leases an inert marker, refuses a production posture); the Google Secret Manager adapter is a separate distribution that does not exist yet

record_contract.genuine_call: EgressResult refuses any provenance with genuine_call other than False (records.py) and stays so until LP-2b is ruled: genuine_call True admitted only for a result produced by a provider adapter that holds a lease whose is_production_authoritative is True, under a production posture, and never from a fixture
record_contract.provider_adapter: ugence_model_egress_unit.provider.EgressProvider; the OpenAI adapter is a separate distribution that does not exist yet and, when it does, may build a request only from the EgressRequest's minimized context, may reach api.openai.com and no other host, takes its credential only through CredentialLease.use, and labels every answer UNTRUSTED_EVIDENCE

must_never_contain: an API key, OAuth token, service-account key or any credential
a prompt, response or any customer content
a fixture recorded as a commissioned adapter
